newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity mixed at close; PV up on weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity mixed at close; PV up on weather.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were mixed at the close, with Palo Verde (PV) contracts garnering some support from expected cold weather, market sources said Monday.
Source said long players were disappointed that electricity did not, after an early spurt, continue to rally along with natural gas and became sellers toward the end of trading.
But forecasts calling for below-normal temperatures in the Rocky Mountain region helped support Southwest prices.
California-Oregon border (COB) contracts, however, were mostly down amid abundant hydroelectric suppies in the Northwest.
After the futures market closed, February COB in the over the counter market was quoted $15.00-15.25 per megawatt hour (MWh), while PV was at $16.75-17.00.
NYMEX February COB settled down 60 cents at $15.25, while March was down 10 cents at $13.80. Other COB contracts were down 10 cents higher to 75 cents lower.
March PV on NYMEX was down 2 cents at $16.98, while March was unchanged at $15.90. Other PV contracts were 5 to 25 cents higher.
